[curious, lively explainer, warm bright timbre, neutral American accent, conversational pace, starts speaking immediately] This machine is almost a light-day away. Next month, it crosses that line, the first thing we ever built to do it. Voyager one launched in nineteen seventy-seven, swung past Jupiter and Saturn, then crossed into interstellar space in twenty twelve. Its radio runs on about twenty watts, a fridge light bulb. Giant dishes on Earth strain to hear it. Its plutonium power fades every year. So engineers keep switching parts off, one by one, just to keep it talking. A radio hello takes nearly a day to reach it. Say hi this morning, and it hears you tomorrow.
